clues: This chief city of Zimbabwe sits on a high plateau in the north east of the land. It is the main town of the Mashonaland region there.
Though it lies in the tropics, a high plateau and cool winds from the south east make it cooler here. Its air stays drier than in most hot lands.
It was founded in 1890 by a small armed force of a British firm. The force was known far and wide as the Pioneer Column.
This town has staged both the All-Africa Games of 1995 and a Cricket World Cup. Sports fans from far lands came here in 1995 and again in 2003.
It is the home of a football club that has won more crowns than any other in its land. That club is a proud mark of sport in this town and its land.
